text:
Maya: heads up — p99 for text-gen routes in us-east jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s over last 3h, customers reporting timeouts. seen correlated increase in prefix cache miss_rate and eviction. filing here for triage
Sam: can you paste the top metrics and customer ids?
Maya: two customer tickets attached (cust-A, cust-B). metrics snippet: 
```
prefix_cache.hit_rate: 0.18
prefix_cache.miss_rate: 0.82
prefix_cache.evictions_per_min: 420
kv_cache.size_bytes: 4.2e9
model.token.latency.p99: 1200ms
```
Logs show a flood of unique cache keys, many created per-request: `prefix_key=/<model>/user/req/trace-<uuid>`
InfraBot: ALERT: route:text-gen-us-east p99 above threshold 1000ms (3h). rollback window ends in 30m.
Alex: quick theory — noticed a gateway change around 02:12 that started forwarding `X-Client-Trace` header to backend. if our prefix-key builder includes all headers by default, per-request tracing header will explode key cardinality. need to confirm.
Jordan: I can repro locally by curling with random X-Client-Trace header. shows new key each request and hotset grows. repro steps: 
```
# reproduce
for i in $(seq 1 100); do 
  curl -s -H "X-Client-Trace: $(uuidgen)" "https://api.redwood.internal/v1/generate?model=redwood-small" > /dev/null
done
# then check cache metrics
kubectl exec -it pod/runtime-0 -- /bin/sh -c "redis-cli HLEN prefix_index"
```
Sam: confirmed — trace header is in the prefix key payload on runtime side. I grepped commit history and found a small gateway PR (merge 0a9b3) that switched header passthrough mode from `whitelist` -> `forward_all` to fix proxied auth for an internal partner.
Maya: customers are impacted now. any mitigation options before rolling back gateway?
Alex: short-term mitigations:
- 1) toggle runtime config to strip high-cardinality headers from cache key builder (`cache.key.header_whitelist = ["user-id","content-type"]`)
- 2) enable `prefix_key_hashing = true` which maps canonicalized keys to 128-bit hash (reduces memory indexing cost)
- 3) raise eviction threshold temporarily to avoid constant churn (danger: memory blowout)
Jordan: I pushed a quick patch to runtime config via admin API to normalize keys and enable hashing. command used: 
```
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/config/cache -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"prefix_key_normalization": true, "prefix_header_whitelist": ["user-id","x-rls"]}'
```
Sam: canary rollout plan: 10% of us-east traffic -> config change for 15m, monitor p95/p99 and evictions, then 50% -> 100% if stable. I started the canary at 17:12 UTC.
Maya: customer comms drafted, Priya please review: "we identified a cache key explosion caused by a gateway header passthrough change leading to higher latency. we pushed a temporary key-normalization config which lowered p99 and we're doing a controlled rollout. will follow up with permanent fix."
Customer Success - Priya: LGTM, adding note to both tickets and offering credits.
InfraBot: METRIC_UPDATE: after canary start: prefix_cache.miss_rate -> 0.39, evictions_per_min -> 120, model.token.latency.p99 -> 320ms
Maya: p99 dropped to ~320ms on canary hosts, that's promising. next steps?
Alex: permanent fix options:
- revert gateway `forward_all` change and instead explicitly whitelist auth headers needed by the partner.
- add runtime unit/integration tests to assert no per-request headers are used in cache keys (CI guard).
- add metric alert for rapid increase in unique prefix keys (delta over 5m).
Sam: created an issue and assigned: ENG-RUNTIME-873, includes rollback PR for gateway and runtime config hardening.
Jordan: deployed full rollout at 17:45 UTC after 3 canary intervals. monitoring now.
InfraBot: RESOLVED_ALERT: route:text-gen-us-east p99 returned below threshold at 18:01 UTC.
Maya: closing loop with customers, adding postmortem notes. lessons: never forward unvetted headers to runtime, and treat header passthrough changes as cache-impacting. also will add a smoke test that simulates random headers and checks key cardinality.
Sam: follow-up action items: 1) gateway revert PR (author: emily) 2) runtime key-builder whitelist + hashing default 3) CI test (simulate header-cardinality) 4) metric alert for unique_keys delta
Maya: thanks all. I'll drop a short postmortem in #postmortems and ping infra to review the gateway policy change process. :thumbsup:
